extracted.intended_audience: vehicle manufacturers, test laboratories, seat/seat-belt suppliers, safety engineers, and regulatory stakeholders performing or assessing FMVSS No. 210 anchorage strength testing
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and test-procedure requirements for evaluating seat belt anchorage strength under FMVSS No. 210, including use and positioning of Force Application Devices (FADs) and pelvic/torso body blocks, preload and test loads, repeatability and validation across vehicle types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preload force for body blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a preload force of 1,335 N to each body block (10% of the full test load) while positioning the torso and pelvic body blocks so a specified 'target' on each block is within the applicable zone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors FMVSS No. 210 laboratory practice of 10% preload; positioning is accomplished while the preload is applied. FMVSS No. 222 uses a 600 N preload for its torso block (approx. 8%–18% of full test load depending on vehicle weight).

rubrics_metrics.name: Body block zone positioning (three-dimensional zones)
rubrics_metrics.description: Position torso and pelvic body blocks within separately-specified three-dimensional zones (one zone for the torso block and one for the pelvic block) with the target on each block inside the applicable zone while preload is applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the preload application is complete, verify that the origin of the torso body block radius at any point across its thickness lies within the defined zone before applying the full test forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body block zone dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified zone dimensions for preload positioning: Pelvic Body Block — Depth 205 mm, Width 340 mm, Height 145 mm; Torso Body Block — Depth 240 mm, Width 530 mm, Height 245 mm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zones were developed by fleet testing, mathematical expansion to four standard deviations in X/Y/Z to cover untested configurations, mirroring for right/center seats, and rounding vertex coordinates up to the nearest 5 mm; precise locations are specified relative to the Seating reference point (SgRP) in the regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAD positioning repeatability/tolerance
rubrics_metrics.description: FAD placement repeatability demonstrated by three technicians placing a FAD in the same vehicle with predetermined measuring points within 1/4 in (6.35 mm) of one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FMVSS No. 208 H-point tolerance is 1/2 in (12.7 mm), so 1/4 in variability for FAD seating is considered reasonable. Use of consistent seating procedure required to achieve this repeatability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeatability of applied forces (statistical assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess repeatability of forces applied to seat belt anchorages using statistical measures (coefficient of variance (CV) for peak values and time-based metrics) and established CV acceptance criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing used a rigid test rig with anchored load cells, a rigid seat substitute, and high-strength webbing in a generic configuration to minimize variability; both peak force values and time-domain metrics should be analyzed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicant test seating arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicant/validation tests may position the FAD1, FAD2, and body blocks in adjacent seating positions (e.g., FAD1 in left seat, torso & pelvic body blocks in right seat, FAD2 in center seat when present) and test every seat in each vehicle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some tests used matched-pair vehicles tested either only with FAD or only with body blocks to address concerns about simultaneous placement effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: FMVSS No. 210 test load and hold time
rubrics_metrics.description: FMVSS No. 210 specifies the full test loads for seat belt anchorages (example cited: 13,345 N) and requires holding the achieved test load for 10 seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare differences with international standards (e.g., ECE R14 has slightly different loads and hold time requirements). Exact FMVSS No. 210 loads are authoritative in the regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECE R14 (UN Regulation No. 14) differences
rubrics_metrics.description: ECE R14 requires a load (example cited: 13,500 N ± 200 N for some categories), allows achieving the load in 60 seconds (vs FMVSS 30 seconds), and has a hold requirement of 0.2 seconds (vs FMVSS 10 seconds). R14 specifies placement of body blocks at preload, belt pulled tight against pelvic block, torso block pushed into seat back while belt pulled tight, and specifies pivot point location on torso block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R14 also specifies distinct pelvic block for side-facing seats and that test load direction be forward relative to vehicle; load magnitudes vary by vehicle category (M1, N1, M3, N3, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport Canada TSD No. 210 positioning procedure (ATD marking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transport Canada uses a 50th percentile ATD to set belt routing (marking webbing with ATD in seat), then places body blocks 'against the back of the seat' and fastens belts around them; blocks are moved forward if the belt buckle seems likely to be damaged but not beyond the ATD mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach addresses buckle interference differently than NHTSA's procedure and demonstrates a procedural option when interference is observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAE J384/J383 alignment and options
rubrics_metrics.description: SAE J384 (2014) is nearly identical to FMVSS No. 210 (similar body block specs, test loads) with a specified preload of 10%; torso block may include a pull arm; belts positioned to 'represent design intent routing'; option to replace seat belt webbing with other material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: J383 provides design recommendations for anchorage locations; this standard can be referenced for test procedure detail and design intent routing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests to failure not required by FMVSS No. 210
rubrics_metrics.description: FMVSS No. 210 does not require testing anchorages to failure and NHTSA does not perform or require tests to failure as part of compliance testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturers that test to failure for their own purposes may choose to replace FAD with body blocks for failure testing if durability of the FAD is a concern; NHTSA will not research FAD materials for non-required destructive testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belt slippage treatment in compliance testing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the seat belt slides off or over the FAD during a compliance test, the test is considered invalid (not a non-compliance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA observed no significant belt movement on the FAD during their tests; commenters asserting slippage must provide data to demonstrate a problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAD material and webbing damage prevention (hip clip design)
rubrics_metrics.description: FAD torso/pelvic portions are molded smooth polyurethane; initial metal hip-clip design caused belt damage in testing and was redesigned with smoother edges; redesigned hip clips prevented webbing damage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hip clip design must avoid sharp edges or features that could cut or abrade webbing; prototypes should be validated to ensure no belt breakage or damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAD weight and handling considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: FAD1 weight: 55.79 kg (123 lb); FAD2 weight: 27.55 kg (47.5 lb). Current body blocks vary: torso ~7.7–13.6 kg, pelvic ~37.9 kg (optional inboard pelvic ~19.5 kg) when aluminum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laboratory lifting policies and technician strength affect handling; NHTSA found FADs generally easier to position and rarely required more than one technician, but manufacturers/test labs may have internal policies requiring additional personnel or mechanical assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAD dimensions and representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: FAD1 dimensions most closely resemble a 50th percentile adult male; FAD2 is a scaled-down FAD1 (shoulder pivot height 60%, shoulder breadth 71%, hip breadth 66% of 50th male). FADs are not modeled to represent a particular ATD occupant category and are intended to assess anchorage performance, not occupant injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If manufacturers are concerned about seat performance with FAD2, they may choose to certify with current body blocks instead; weight alone is not indicative of which occupant category a FAD represents because FADs lack limbs and head.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zone validation across vehicle types and extremes
rubrics_metrics.description: Zones were validated via multi-phase research: indicant anchorage tests on nine vehicles (varied vehicle sizes), matched-pair testing with only FAD or only body blocks, systematic testing across five passenger vehicles with parameter variation, mirroring coordinates for right/center positions, expansion to ±4 standard deviations, indicant tests at longitudinal extremes, and validation in heavy-duty vehicles (school buses and motorcoach seats).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These steps are intended to ensure practicability and repeatability of zones across a wide range of vehicle types and seating configurations and to provide defensible zone boundaries for the regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test setup standardization to minimize variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeatability analyses used standardized setups: anchorage load cells mounted to a rigid test rig, vehicle seat replaced with a rigid seat, seat belt webbing replaced with high-strength webbing, and generic configurations to minimize variability in results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use controlled, repeatable test fixtures and configurations when assessing force repeatability; perform multiple repeats and analyze CV to rate channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for adjusting pelvic block for buckle interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the pelvic block interferes with the belt buckle, blocks may be moved forward if inspection indicates potential buckle damage, but not beyond the position marked using an ATD (Transport Canada approach).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adjustment method differs from NHTSA's procedure (NHTSA specifies zone-based positioning); incorporate a documented marking/limit if adopting an ATD-based adjustment method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position verification before applying full test loads
rubrics_metrics.description: After applying preload and positioning, verify that the torso and pelvic body blocks (e.g., origin of torso body block radius) are within the specified zone boundaries before applying the required test forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This verification is a prerequisite to ensure consistent starting geometry; once verified, apply the full test loads and hold as specified by the applicable standard (e.g., FMVSS No. 210).

rubrics_metrics.name: Zone boundary reference and coordinate rounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Zones and their precise locations are specified in relation to the Seating reference point (SgRP); vertex coordinates were rounded up to the nearest 5 mm for ease of use in the regulatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text and figures provide exact SgRP-referenced coordinates and depictions; use the rounded coordinates for practical placement, recognizing they were intentionally conservative to accommodate future vehicle designs.
